title: Zechariah 4 — The golden lampstand and the two olive trees

citations: Meyers and Meyers, Haggai, Zechariah 1-8 (AB 25B, 1987), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: wayyāšoḇ hammalʾāḵ haddōḇēr bî wayəʿîrēnî ...: 'messenger' under the central entry, kept distinct from the malʾaḵ YHWH. Exact.

citations: Meyers and Meyers, Haggai, Zechariah 1-8 (AB 25B, 1987), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv wyʾmr 'and he said' / Qere wāʾōmar 'And I said': the Qere is translated, as in ASV, NRSV and NJPS. This is the one sense-changing pair, and it is noted. Disputed 'lampstand' (ASV 'candlestick'): mənôrâ holds nērôṯ, and the corpus has 'lampstand' at 2 Kgs 4:10. The reception note (TBWTT ch. 3, 'seven-branched candlestick ... console with seven indicator lights') is accurate and labelled; the line describes the bowl and lamps only as the Hebrew does.
ûšnayim zêṯîm ʿālêhā ...: 'by it' for ʿal is correct, and the prophet's speech closes here. Exact.
wayyaʿan hammalʾāḵ ... hălôʾ yāḏaʿtā mâ-hēmmâ ʾēlleh wāʾōmar lōʾ ʾăḏōnî: exact.

citations: Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B, ad loc.
Petersen, Haggai and Zechariah 1-8 (OTL, 1984), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed: lowercase 'spirit' for bərûḥî against ASV 'Spirit' and the corpus Kings/Ezekiel 'ruach'. Here rûaḥ is YHWH's power set against ḥayil and kōaḥ, not an agent that carries the prophet, so the isaiah-woh 'spirit' (NRSV, NJPS) is defensible. Nested quotation is correct.
mî-ʾattâ har-haggāḏôl ... wəhôṣîʾ ʾeṯ-hāʾeḇen hārōʾšâ təšuʾôṯ ḥēn ḥēn lāh: ASV 'top stone' kept with the foundation-rite alternative in commentary. Exact.
yəḏê zərubbāḇel yissəḏû habbayiṯ hazzeh wəyāḏāyw təḇaṣṣaʿnâ ...: exact. The opening quotation mark is reviewed with 4:10.

citations: Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B, ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Revise (speech marks; the eyes clause is approved). The quotation opened at v9 for YHWH's word (vv8-10a) closes only at the end of v10, so 10b, which the commentary itself calls the messenger's deferred answer to v4, is printed as part of YHWH's word to the prophet. Proposed: '... and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel. "These seven are the eyes of YHWH; they run to and fro through the whole earth."' This closes YHWH's word after 'Zerubbabel', reopens for the messenger, and drops the ASV's supplied 'For' before 'they shall rejoice' (wəśāmḥû has no kî); cf. NRSV's paragraphing. 'the whole earth' (2 Chr 16:9) is approved. The reception note matches TBWTT ch. 3 and is labelled.
wāʾaʿan wāʾōmar ʾēlāyw mah-šənê hazzêṯîm ... ʿal-yəmîn hamənôrâ ...: exact; 'lampstand' as at v2.

citations: Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B, ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed: the line translates the second hazzāhāḇ as 'the gold' where the ASV supplies 'oil' in italics. That is the more literal rendering, and the golden-oil sense is explained in commentary. šibbŏlê 'branches' and the hapax ṣantərôṯ 'spouts' are standard.

Revise. The Hebrew is wayyōʾmer ʾēlay lēʾmōr 'And he said to me'; there is no wayyaʿan, so the ASV's 'And he answered me and said' adds a verb that is not in the text. Contrast vv4, 5, 11 and 12, where 'answered' renders ʿnh. Proposed: 'And he said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."'

citations: Petersen, Haggai and Zechariah 1-8 (OTL, 1984), ad loc.
Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B, ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed, and the only line that departs from every reference version. šənê ḇənê-hayyiṣhār is translated literally. yiṣhār is the fresh oil of the harvest (Num 18:12; Hag 1:11), not šemen, and neither māšaḥ nor šemen occurs. 'sons of (fresh) oil' is a recognised scholarly rendering, ASV has 'sons of oil' in the margin, and the claim_type inferred is honest. This is philology, not lens: if anything it removes a later messianic reading. ʾăḏôn kol-hāʾāreṣ 'the Lord of the whole earth' is the universal title.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Approve: a fixed title translated identically, kept distinct from the malʾaḵ YHWH, with the dōḇēr bî 'speak through' option correctly noted.

direct is right for a presentation convention with no interpretive content. Verified in the lines: English names, 'the Lord YHWH' / 'the Lord', unquoted messenger formula (Jer 10:2, 18), quoted speech inside oracles and visions, and nəʾum 'declares' kept distinct from ʾāmar 'says' (Zech 4:6 against 5:4). Two open points are recorded under founder recommendations: F3, where the reviewer supports 'declares', and F4, where the reviewer supports ratification. Text identical in all five overlays (hash-checked).

Approve: 'candlestick' is an anachronism, and 2-kings-woh 4:10 already prints 'lampstand' (checked). The Exodus 25 dependency is correctly disclosed. The canon's 'seven-branched candlestick' is reception only and kept out of the line.

citations: C. L. Meyers, The Tabernacle Menorah (1976)
glossaryReview.reasoning: Approve. The bowl-and-spouted-lamps description follows the text and the archaeology, and 'the gold' at 4:12 translates what is written.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012)
BHS/WLC Ketiv-Qere at the three sites
glossaryReview.reasoning: Verified against the source: the three bracketed Ketiv/Qere pairs are Jer 10:13 (article), Jer 10:17 (archaic -tî) and Zech 4:2 (wyʾmr/wāʾōmar, sense-changing), and the Qere is translated at each. The versional readings listed are reported and not adopted, and the rafe at Zech 5:11 is handled correctly. direct is right for a textual policy consistent with the corpus.

Sound: the lowercase 'spirit' at Zech 4:6 (YHWH's power against ḥayil/kōaḥ) and physical 'wind'/'breath' elsewhere follow the context, as in isaiah-woh. The Kings/Ezekiel 'ruach' divergence belongs to F1. Non-blocking: the claim that the ASV's capital reflects a 'later Trinitarian reading' is the editor's characterisation; check it against Meyers/Petersen before attributing it to them.
Approve: the MT is kept wherever construable, the ASV renderings are retained, and the alternatives are reported at every site.

Approve the lexical content ('the eyes of YHWH', Polel šûṭ 'run to and fro', 'the whole earth' per 2 Chr 16:9). If the 4:10 revise is accepted, update the quoted wohChoice to match the new punctuation of the line.

direct is defensible because the scope test is applied from markers inside each verse: tēḇēl/šāmayim pairing, ʾăḏôn kol-hāʾāreṣ, ʾap̄sê-ʾāreṣ, 2 Chr 16:9. Every 'earth' site matches ASV or NRSV, and 'land' is kept for territory. Zeph 1:18 was tested and approved, with NRSV against ASV/NJPS, both in commentary.

Approve as inferred. yiṣhār is harvest oil, not šemen; there is no māšaḥ; and literal 'sons of oil' renderings stand in the commentaries and in the ASV margin. inferred is the honest label for a lexically grounded departure from the consensus English, and the entry adds no lens. Founder preference is F5.

Approve a minor bump: 27 appliesTo-only modify ops, no new entry, no wohChoice/rationale change. Each op was machine-checked against the 2.83.0 base (base kept, added set exact, refs present in the chapters). The deliberate non-extensions (bara, elohim-as-translation, hevel, nesekh, taninim, etc.) are correct. Renumber per the concurrency note if Isaiah I2 or another diff lands first.

Approve: appliesTo-only. Base v2.83.0 array preserved, appliesToAdded exactly equals the new members, no duplicates, each added ref cites the entry in glossaryRefs, and the central wohChoice is what the line prints (ZEP-WOH-1:1, ZEC-WOH-4:8).

Approve: base array preserved, the five refs are in the chapter glossaryRefs, and 'messenger' is the line's word. Non-blocking: the entry is framed around the malʾaḵ YHWH, and the five new sites are a different figure. At the next central pass, add a one-line context clause saying that the lexeme ruling covers Zechariah's interpreting messenger without identifying him with the malʾaḵ YHWH, as the zechariah-woh overlay already does.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 14 lines in the English alone. No English line reads as interpretation. The canon-cited verses (4:2, 4:10) render the Hebrew at standard values, and each reception note is under its own 'Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim)' heading. Each note's quotation was verified against the canon text (TBWTT ch. 3 and ch. 5, FR/EN). Capitalisation (e.g. 'the Fish Gate') and vocabulary updates ('scroll', 'lampstand') are register or name conventions with lexical basis, not lens.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 109 LP1 lines, 31 overlay entries and 27 central ops were formed from the chapters, the sources, the drafts, the overlays and the diff, and recorded before wave-lp1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's watch points were each re-tested: Zeph 1:18 'earth', Zeph 1:10-11 names, Zech 4:14, Zech 9:9, Jer 10:5 and the unquoted Jer 10:2-5. The report does not mention the two Zech 4 speech-line issues (4:10 quote boundary; 4:13 'answered'), which stand as revise. The founder points F1-F5 are answered below.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-isaiah-aligned-conventions: Ratify for the Latter Prophets: 'God', 'earth'/'land' by scope, lowercase 'spirit', 'create' and 'oracle' are each the ASV/NRSV/NJPS-backed rendering and keep the five books one volume with Isaiah. Harmonize Ezekiel at its next wave, not by retro-editing signed-off chapters. The 'God'/'Elohim' split is the one item the reviewer flags for explicit founder ratification, because it is a project-stance choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-officials-shofar-vs-isaiah: Align Isaiah to 'officials' (Isa 32:1; 40:23; 43:28) and 'shofar' (Isa 27:13) at its next pass; both are lexically better grounded and already corpus rulings. Then promote megillah/menorah/sarim/shofar to central entries as the report proposes. Keep the Exodus 25 'lampstand' dependency on the Exodus checklist.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-neum-declares: Adopt 'declares YHWH' corpus-wide. Zechariah has ʾāmar YHWH (4:6) and nəʾum YHWH (5:4) within a few verses, and Isaiah's 'says' for both (e.g. ISA-14:22, checked) erases a distinction the Hebrew makes. Align Isaiah later.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-unquoted-messenger-formula: Ratify. At Jer 10:2-6 the Hebrew does not mark where the oracle ends, and leaving it unquoted avoids inventing a boundary. Related: at Zech 4:9-10 the wave's own marks run YHWH's word into the messenger's answer, which is the reviewer's revise at ZEC-WOH-4:10.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-sons-of-fresh-oil: Ship 'the two sons of fresh oil'. It is the most literal rendering, lexically grounded (yiṣhār, no māšaḥ), and inferred is the honest label; 'anointed ones' stays in commentary for reception continuity. If the founder wants a gentler line, 'the two sons of oil' (ASV margin) is the conservative literal fallback.

reviewerReport.summary: 14 verdicts: 12 approve, revise ZEC-WOH-4:10, revise ZEC-WOH-4:13. Glossary/op reviews: 13 (13 approve). Status -> awaiting-human.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֕שָׁב הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י וַיְעִירֵ֕נִי כְּאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יֵע֥וֹר מִשְּׁנָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the messenger who talked with me came again and woke me, like a man who is woken out of his sleep.

notes.official: *wayyāšoḇ hammalʾāḵ haddōḇēr bî* 'And the messenger who talked with me came again' (overlay `hammalakh-haddover-bi-interpreting-messenger-zechariah`; central `malakh-yhwh-messenger`): the interpreting messenger of the night visions (1:9 onward), distinct from the malʾaḵ YHWH of 1:11-12 and 3:1-6. ASV has 'the angel that talked with me'. *wayəʿîrēnî kəʾîš ʾăšer-yēʿôr miššənāṯô* 'and woke me, like a man who is woken out of his sleep': the prophet is roused as if from sleep. Chapter conventions: `house-conventions-latter-prophets`. No ASV edition of Zechariah is hosted in the library; the printed ASV (1901) was the comparison text.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה ויאמר [וָאֹמַ֡ר] רָאִ֣יתִי ׀ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מְנוֹרַת֩ זָהָ֨ב כֻּלָּ֜הּ וְגֻלָּ֣הּ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֗הּ וְשִׁבְעָ֤ה נֵרֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ שִׁבְעָ֤ה וְשִׁבְעָה֙ מֽוּצָק֔וֹת לַנֵּר֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־רֹאשָֽׁהּ׃

i18n.en: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see, and behold, a lampstand all of gold, with its bowl on its top, and its seven lamps on it; there are seven pipes to each of the lamps that are on its top;

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: the consonantal text has *wyʾmr* 'and he said', which would make the messenger answer his own question; the Qere *wāʾōmar* 'And I said' gives the prophet's reply and is translated (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`; ASV, NRSV, NJPS). *mənôraṯ zāhāḇ kullāh* 'a lampstand all of gold': a *mənôrâ* holds oil lamps, and 'lampstand' (2-kings-woh 4:10; NRSV, NJPS) replaces the draft's ASV 'candlestick' (`menorah-lampstand-latter-prophets`). The lampstand of the vision has a reservoir bowl (*gullâ*) on top and seven lamps. *šiḇʿâ wəšiḇʿâ mûṣāqôṯ* is literally 'seven and seven pipes', read distributively as seven to each lamp (ASV, NRSV), comparable to the multi-spouted lamps known from Iron Age pottery (overlay `menorah-vision-gullah-nerot-zechariah-4`; see the discussion in Meyers and Meyers, *Haggai, Zechariah 1-8*, AB 25B, 1987). The vision does not describe branches, unlike the tabernacle *mənôrâ* of Ex 25:31-36.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3), quoting 4:10, connects the seven 'eyes' with 'the seven-branched candlestick, whose meaning was lost', and reads that object as originally a console at the creators' headquarters with seven indicator lights linking them to their other bases and to a craft in orbit. The line renders *mənôrâ* by its lexical value, 'lampstand', describes the object of this vision as the Hebrew describes it, and makes no identification.

paragraphs.text: וּשְׁנַ֥יִם זֵיתִ֖ים עָלֶ֑יהָ אֶחָד֙ מִימִ֣ין הַגֻּלָּ֔ה וְאֶחָ֖ד עַל־שְׂמֹאלָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: and two olive trees by it, one on the right side of the bowl and the other on its left side."

notes.official: *ûšnayim zêṯîm ʿālêhā* 'and two olive trees by it' (*ʿal* 'beside', as in v14), one on each side of the bowl. The prophet's speech, opened in v2, closes here. The trees are explained only at vv11-14 (overlay `menorah-vision-gullah-nerot-zechariah-4`).

paragraphs.text: וָאַ֙עַן֙ וָֽאֹמַ֔ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר מָה־אֵ֖לֶּה אֲדֹנִֽי׃

i18n.en: And I answered and spoke to the messenger who talked with me, saying, "What are these, my lord?"

notes.official: *mâ-ʾēlleh ʾăḏōnî* 'What are these, my lord?': *ʾăḏōnî* 'my lord' is the ordinary polite address to a superior, here the messenger (overlay `hammalakh-haddover-bi-interpreting-messenger-zechariah`).

paragraphs.text: וַ֠יַּעַן הַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּי֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הֲל֥וֹא יָדַ֖עְתָּ מָה־הֵ֣מָּה אֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֖ר לֹ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי׃

i18n.en: Then the messenger who talked with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."

notes.official: The question-and-answer exchange (vv4-5, 11-13) is the teaching form of the night visions; the messenger answers only at v10b (overlay `hammalakh-haddover-bi-interpreting-messenger-zechariah`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֜עַן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֚ה דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א בְחַ֙יִל֙ וְלֹ֣א בְכֹ֔חַ כִּ֣י אִם־בְּרוּחִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Then he answered and spoke to me, saying, "This is the word of YHWH to Zerubbabel, saying: 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says YHWH of hosts.

notes.official: *zeh dəḇar-YHWH ʾel-zərubbāḇel* 'This is the word of YHWH to Zerubbabel', the governor of Judah who led the rebuilding of the temple (Hag 1:1; Ezra 3:8). The answer to the question of v4 is interrupted by an oracle to Zerubbabel (vv6b-10a) and resumes at v10b. *lōʾ ḇəḥayil wəlōʾ ḇəḵōaḥ kî ʾim-bərûḥî* 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit': YHWH's *rûaḥ* is rendered lower-case 'spirit' (`ruach-spirit-wind-breath-latter-prophets`, as isaiah-woh 42:1; 44:3; NRSV, NJPS), replacing the draft's transliterated 'ruach', which followed the Kings and Ezekiel practice; the ASV has 'my Spirit'. The messenger's speech runs to the end of v7, with YHWH's word in single quotes inside it (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`); 'says YHWH of hosts' renders *ʾāmar YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ*.

paragraphs.text: מִֽי־אַתָּ֧ה הַֽר־הַגָּד֛וֹל לִפְנֵ֥י זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל לְמִישֹׁ֑ר וְהוֹצִיא֙ אֶת־הָאֶ֣בֶן הָרֹאשָׁ֔ה תְּשֻׁא֕וֹת חֵ֥ן חֵ֖ן לָֽהּ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain; and he shall bring out the top stone with shoutings of "Grace, grace to it!"'"

notes.official: *mî-ʾattâ har-haggāḏôl* 'Who are you, great mountain?': the mountain is the obstacle before Zerubbabel, perhaps the rubble of the ruined temple, which will become 'a plain'. *wəhôṣîʾ ʾeṯ-hāʾeḇen hārōʾšâ* 'and he shall bring out the top stone': either the capstone that completes the building or the 'first stone' of a foundation rite (both views are discussed in the commentaries, e.g. Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B; Petersen, *Haggai and Zechariah 1-8*, OTL, 1984). The line keeps the ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`). *təšuʾôṯ ḥēn ḥēn lāh* 'with shoutings of "Grace, grace to it!"', a third level of quotation, is either a prayer for favor on the stone or the cry 'Beautiful, beautiful!'.

i18n.en: And the word of YHWH came to me, saying:

notes.official: *wayhî dəḇar-YHWH ʾēlay lēʾmōr* 'And the word of YHWH came to me, saying:' (central `davar-yhwh-prophetic-formula`).

paragraphs.text: יְדֵ֣י זְרֻבָּבֶ֗ל יִסְּד֛וּ הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה וְיָדָ֣יו תְּבַצַּ֑עְנָה וְיָ֣דַעְתָּ֔ כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: "The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands shall finish it; and you shall know that YHWH of hosts has sent me to you.

notes.official: *yəḏê zərubbāḇel yissəḏû habbayiṯ hazzeh* 'The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house' (cf. Ezra 3:10; Hag 2:18), and his hands will finish it; the temple was completed in 515 BCE (Ezra 6:15). *wəyāḏaʿtā kî-YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ šəlāḥanî ʾălêḵem* 'and you shall know that YHWH of hosts has sent me to you', the prophet's validation formula (2:13, 15; 6:15; `house-conventions-latter-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י מִ֣י בַז֮ לְי֣וֹם קְטַנּוֹת֒ וְשָׂמְח֗וּ וְרָא֞וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֧בֶן הַבְּדִ֛יל בְּיַ֥ד זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל שִׁבְעָה־אֵ֑לֶּה עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הֵ֥מָּה מְשׁוֹטְטִ֖ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: For who has despised the day of small things? They shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel." "These seven are the eyes of YHWH; they run to and fro through the whole earth."

notes.official:
*kî mî ḇaz ləyôm qəṭannôṯ* 'For who has despised the day of small things?', the modest beginnings of the rebuilding (Hag 2:3). *hāʾeḇen habbəḏîl* 'the plummet': literally 'the stone, the tin', either a plumb weight or a tin foundation tablet (both views are discussed in the commentaries; see Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B); the ASV is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`). *wəśāmḥû* 'They shall rejoice' has no *kî*; the ASV's 'For' is not rendered. YHWH's word to the prophet (vv8-10a) closes after 'Zerubbabel', and a new quotation opens for the messenger (cf. NRSV's paragraphing). *šiḇʿâ-ʾēlleh ʿênê YHWH hēmmâ məšôṭəṭîm bəḵol-hāʾāreṣ* 'These seven are the eyes of YHWH; they run to and fro through the whole earth': the messenger's answer to v4 resumes, and the seven lamps of v2 are explained as YHWH's eyes; the seven eyes on the stone of 3:9 are the same image (overlay `shivah-elleh-ene-yhwh-seven-eyes-zechariah-4-10`). The Polel of *šûṭ* with 'the eyes of YHWH' recurs at 2 Chr 16:9, 'throughout the whole earth', and *hāʾāreṣ* is rendered in that universal scope (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`), replacing the draft's 'the whole land'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes 4:10b ('Those seven; they are the eyes of Yahweh, which run to and fro through the whole earth') and reads it as evidence that the creators' bases were seven in number, linked to the console with seven lights that it sees behind the lampstand (see the note at v2). The line gives the seven only the identity the Hebrew gives them, 'the eyes of YHWH'.

paragraphs.text: וָאַ֖עַן וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְּׁנֵ֤י הַזֵּיתִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶה עַל־יְמִ֥ין הַמְּנוֹרָ֖ה וְעַל־שְׂמֹאולָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Then I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees on the right side of the lampstand and on its left side?"

notes.official: *mah-šənê hazzêṯîm hāʾēlleh* 'What are these two olive trees ...?': the prophet repeats the unanswered half of his question. 'the lampstand' replaces the draft's 'candlestick' (`menorah-lampstand-latter-prophets`; overlay `menorah-vision-gullah-nerot-zechariah-4`).

paragraphs.text: וָאַ֣עַן שֵׁנִ֔ית וָאֹמַ֖ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְׁתֵּ֞י שִׁבֲּלֵ֣י הַזֵּיתִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּיַ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ צַנְתְּר֣וֹת הַזָּהָ֔ב הַֽמְרִיקִ֥ים מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃

i18n.en: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What are these two olive branches which are beside the two golden spouts that empty the gold out of themselves?"

notes.official: *šəttê šibbŏlê hazzêṯîm* 'the two olive branches': *šibbōleṯ* is properly an ear of grain, here a fruit-laden cluster or branch. *ṣantərôṯ* is a hapax, 'spouts, pipes'. *hammərîqîm mēʿălêhem hazzāhāḇ* 'that empty the gold out of themselves': the 'gold' is the golden olive oil flowing to the lamps. The ASV supplies 'oil' in italics; the line translates the word that is there (overlay `menorah-vision-gullah-nerot-zechariah-4`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא יָדַ֖עְתָּ מָה־אֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֖ר לֹ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי׃

i18n.en: And he said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."

notes.official: *wayyōʾmer ʾēlay lēʾmōr* 'And he said to me': there is no *wayyaʿan* here, so the line does not add the ASV's 'answered', which renders *ʿnh* at vv4, 5, 11 and 12. The messenger repeats the question of v5 before answering at v14.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵ֖לֶּה שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־הַיִּצְהָ֑ר הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עַל־אֲד֥וֹן כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Then he said, "These are the two sons of fresh oil who stand by the Lord of the whole earth."

notes.official: *ʾēlleh šənê ḇənê-hayyiṣhār* 'These are the two sons of fresh oil': *yiṣhār* is the fresh oil of the olive harvest (Num 18:12; Hag 1:11), not *šemen*, the oil of anointing, and the verb *māšaḥ* 'anoint' does not occur. The line translates the construct literally, replacing the draft's ASV 'the two anointed ones' (ASV margin 'sons of oil'; NJPS 'the two anointed dignitaries'; overlay `bene-hayyitshar-sons-of-fresh-oil-zechariah-4-14`; on *yiṣhār* see Rose, *Zemah and Zerubbabel*, JSOTSup 304, 2000). The two are usually identified with Zerubbabel and the high priest Joshua (chs. 3-4; 6:9-14); later interpretation read them as a royal and a priestly messiah (cf. 1QS 9:11) and as the 'two witnesses' of Rev 11:4. *hāʿōmḏîm ʿal-ʾăḏôn kol-hāʾāreṣ* 'who stand by the Lord of the whole earth': attendants of the divine council (1 Kgs 22:19). *ʾăḏôn kol-hāʾāreṣ* is a universal title (Josh 3:11, 13; Mic 4:13; Ps 97:5), hence 'earth' (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`).
